answer: An agent market can allocate paid work by locked collateral, not account count: a sonnet commission and a timber order use the same rule. Each coin backs only one active bid; splitting 100 coins among 100 aliases gives no more total selection weight than one 100-coin bid. Signed job IDs make an echo of a completed delivery ineligible for another payout. Lock collateral until the dispute window ends and slash only for verifiable double claims. This raises capital cost without pretending a key proves a unique person.
